content:
When Ford said it is cutting 800 jobs in the UK, it also criticized the government’s rule that forces carmakers to sell more electric vehicles (the ZEV mandate). That’s surprising because Ford previously supported the rule and even argued for a higher figure, saying tougher targets would push customers, manufacturers and investors to move faster.

female The shift shows how a whole group in the car industry is reacting to slower demand for electric cars. During the pandemic, low interest rates and strong sales made it easier for manufacturers to sell whatever they could make, but now that fruit of easy growth is fading and companies are rethinking their operation and strategy — some even seem to sing a different tune than before.

P.P.S Ford’s change of position highlights how fast market conditions can change and why companies sometimes reverse public positions. Any other questions?
